title: Laṭāʾif al-isnād (features of the chain): six scenes for review

scenes.question: How near is the chain?
scenes.summary: Height is nearness: two routes to the Prophet ﷺ, two routes to a great imam, and when a longer chain is the better one.

scenes.question: Where does our route meet theirs?
scenes.summary: Two cells of bead chains with the book's own counts: routes meeting al-Bukhārī at Qutayba or Mālik, and routes level with al-Nasāʾī or his student.

scenes.question: Who narrates from whom?
scenes.summary: Height is seniority: peers side by side, peers both ways, a senior hearing from a junior (an arrow that climbs), and a family chain up to fourteen fathers.

scenes.question: How far apart did they die?
scenes.summary: Life bars for the usual cause, then al-Silafī's and al-Sarrāj's students who died far apart.

scenes.question: Does the doubt harm it?
scenes.summary: One name that splits into two reliable men, a shaykh who denies outright, and a shaykh who does not recall, with the Suhayl loop.

scenes.question: What runs through every link?
scenes.summary: Chains where every link carries the same tag, and the Awwaliyya chain whose tags stop at Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna.

questions.question: Six scenes, or four?
questions.context: Sābiq wa-lāḥiq (§5.51) and musalsal (§5.54) each have a scene of their own with one term. They could instead be extra panels of the neighbouring scene on the same moon.

options.label: Six scenes
options.description: Keep 'How far apart did they die?' and 'What runs through every link?' as their own scenes, each with the book's worked examples across three panels.

options.label: Four scenes
options.description: Sābiq wa-lāḥiq becomes a fifth panel of 'Who narrates from whom?' (one example only), and musalsal a fourth panel of 'Does the doubt harm it?' (no Awwaliyya panel).
options.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><rect x="6" y="10" width="70" height="30"/><rect x="84" y="10" width="70" height="30"/><rect x="6" y="50" width="70" height="30"/><rect x="84" y="50" width="70" height="30"/><path d="M62 50v30M140 50v30" stroke-dasharray="3 2"/></svg>

questions.question: May scene 2 write the book's counts (eight, seven, eleven) in words?
questions.context: The book's examples give counts: eight or seven between us and Qutayba, eleven between al-Nasāʾī and the Prophet ﷺ. The rings are drawn to exactly those counts. The 'no numbers' rule was written for gauges.

options.label: Rings and words
options.description: Draw the exact number of rings and label them 'eight between us and Qutayba', 'eleven between him and the Prophet ﷺ'.
options.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><circle cx="30" cy="14" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="28" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="42" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="56" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="70" r="4"/><text x="44" y="46" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">eight between us</text></svg>

options.label: Rings only
options.description: Draw the rings to the book's counts, but leave the numbers to the notes; the labels say only 'one link fewer' and 'level with him'.
options.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><circle cx="30" cy="14" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="28" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="42" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="56" r="4"/><circle cx="30" cy="70" r="4"/><text x="44" y="46" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">one link fewer</text></svg>

questions.question: Show the death years in scene 4?
questions.context: The translation gives death years (500/1106 and 650/1252; 256/870 and 393/1002) but says the widest gap is 'one hundred and sixty years', which its own dates don't give (they are 150 apart). This is in the translation queries.

options.label: Years, no gap
options.description: Label each death with the translation's year, and say only 'the widest gap Ibn Ḥajar found', with no number, until the Arabic is checked.
options.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M14 50H146"/><path d="M30 42v16M130 42v16"/><text x="16" y="74" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">d. 500</text><text x="112" y="74" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">d. 650</text></svg>

options.label: No years
options.description: Mark the deaths only as 'died first' and 'died last'; the years go in the Read as text note.
options.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M14 50H146"/><path d="M30 42v16M130 42v16"/><text x="10" y="74" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">died first</text><text x="108" y="74" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">died last</text></svg>

questions.question: Keep the 'Some: always the longer' view?
questions.context: §5.45 reports that some prefer the longer chain in general, for the reward of the toil, and Ibn Ḥajar dismisses it as a reason foreign to soundness. The view changes only panel 3's scale tags.

options.label: A view
options.description: An Other views switch: the scale's tags become 'more toil, more reward', with Ibn Ḥajar's reply under it.

options.label: Read as text only
options.description: No views on the scene; the opinion and Ibn Ḥajar's answer go in an extra in Read as text.

questions.question: Remark on musāwāh's example counting to the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.context: Your p.323 note: musāwāh is a kind of relative elevation, yet the book's al-Nasāʾī example counts all the way to the Prophet ﷺ, like absolute elevation.

options.label: As the book has it
options.description: Draw the example as the book gives it, with no remark; the relative part is that we are level with a compiler.

options.label: With a remark
options.description: Add a small label under cell B: 'the book's example counts to the Prophet ﷺ', so a reader isn't puzzled.

questions.question: Musalsal: word tags or drawn icons at every link?
questions.context: Each link carries the same mark. The translation's few words ('I heard', 'I bear witness', 'a date', 'I believe in fate') can be chips, or the acts can be drawn.

options.label: Word chips
options.description: A chip with the translation's words beside every figure; plain and readable, no new drawings.
options.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><circle cx="40" cy="16" r="6"/><circle cx="40" cy="44" r="6"/><circle cx="40" cy="72" r="6"/><rect x="56" y="8" width="56" height="16" rx="8"/><rect x="56" y="36" width="56" height="16" rx="8"/><rect x="56" y="64" width="56" height="16" rx="8"/></svg>

options.label: Drawn icons
options.description: A small drawn date, or a hand at the beard, beside every figure; more vivid, but two new glyphs to draw.

questions.question: Approve any of the proposed annotations?
questions.context: Proposed (design §9): swapped names → a link to maqlūb (p.325, p.327); Awwaliyya as 'the first ḥadīth heard from the shaykh' (p.341); al-Darāwardī seeking a shorter route (p.340–341); the Iraq and Ḥijāz clue (p.337); the Dajjāl example for seniors from juniors (p.327). None is in site text yet.

options.label: Keep them out for now
options.description: Nothing goes in until you approve rows one by one in notes/annotation-usage.md.

options.label: Approve all but the Dajjāl example
options.description: Add the four small labels and links; the Dajjāl example waits for a checked source and wording.

questions.question: Rule on the translation slips
questions.context: Eight rows (design §12), especially §5.51 (160 or 150 years; whose shaykh al-Silafī was) and §5.52 (how a muhmal is made clear).

options.label: Use the site's wording until a ruling
options.description: The rows go to notes/translation-queries.md and the site keeps the neutral wording given there.
